chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
In the hadith of Barirah: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Aishah: 'Free her, for the manumission right (walayah) belongs to the one who frees.'

key_terms.بَرِيرَةَ: Barirah, a female slave mentioned in prophetic traditions

ai.seo_question: Who has the right of manumission (walayah) when a slave is freed?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s directive to Aishah concerning Barirah, establishing the legal maxim that *al-wala’* (the right of manumission and resulting kinship) belongs to the one who frees the slave, irrespective of who provided the financial compensation. This principle is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for determining inheritance rights and social ties between master and freed slave, emphasizing that the act of liberation, not the expenditure, confers the status of *mawla*. The incident also underscores the Prophet’s emphasis on the spiritual and legal dignity of the freed individual within the community.
